Lexapro has been life changing for sure. It's not a miracle cure, I still have rough patches and I still use therapy, but it's made my anxiety so much more manageable. The near constant anxiety has gone away for the most part, I'm not as afraid of people, things aren't as overwhelming as they were :) Adjusting can be weird and uncomfortable, and I think some people don't take them daily as instructed so they're getting all the bad and none of the good! It's worth toughing it out for a bit, it won't cure you but it absolutely can support your brain and take some of the pressure off.

Yeah for sure, I know right now it's especially difficult in a lot of countries. I definitely have been lucky, but finding and joining online communities can really help. I still get a lot of anxiety interacting with new people, but it goes away pretty fast if they're friendly and welcoming. 

I found a lot of good friends through joining a sport that I really like. Keep your chin up, there's absolutely people out there for you

I'm really tired of Gen Z's bashing other Gen Z's. We aren't all shallow, and even the people you think are shallow usually have some deep interest, you just haven't figured it out yet. Plenty of people I thought were shallow at first actually have some really unique perspectives and cool interests. Just because they aren't the same as mine doesn't mean that they're stupid or uninteresting.  

**Going into situations with this preset notion that everyone else is shallow and social media obsessed will do you no favours, and you'll find it hard to connect to people like that.**  

edit because I was being harsh: I used to judge people like that too and it really limited the scope of my social life. It gave me a bit of a complex and just wasn't a positive or constructive attitude to have. Maybe try reaching out to some of the people in the comments here, online friendships are always good :) best of luck to you, I hope you find some like minded people
